title: kv-microvacuum-and-spill-shard-balancer
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: production KV cache observed sustained fragmentation under mixed-length workloads (short-lived small keys mixed with large sequence entries). Existing slab/segment reclamation was heavy-weight and ran only on full GC cycles, which caused reactive spill storms and bursty IO during busy continuous-batching periods. This PR introduces two complementary subsystems: (1) a lightweight "microvacuum" that opportunistically compacts small fragmented allocations during quiet windows without global stops, and (2) a spill-shard-balancer that shards outgoing spill work across multiple spill queues and backpressure levels to avoid single-queue hotspots.

What changed (summary): added a low-overhead microvacuum engine that walks per-tenant small-object free lists, coalesces adjacent fragments, and issues in-place relocation for hot fragments when beneficial. The microvacuum is scheduler-aware: it registers with the runtime scheduler to avoid running during tight continuous-batching windows and to yield on latency pressure. The spill-shard-balancer partitions spill targets by tenant pressure, bandwidth cost, and sequence-length distribution to spread IO and smooth spillback latency. The balancer also exposes per-shard admission controls that the autoscaler and dedicated pools can use to prioritize urgent tenants.

Key design details and trade-offs: microvacuum is designed to keep a small working set (configurable max pages per cycle) and to operate incrementally. It prefers relocating short-lived objects into prewarmed mini-slabs instead of triggering large compactions. This reduces the chance of creating large tails in the KV free map. To avoid jittering allocation patterns we add a fragmentation score tracker and require stable improvement thresholds before promoting aggressive compaction. The spill-shard-balancer uses a lightweight consistent hashing scheme with hot-key hints; it is tolerant of shard leader failover and preserves tenant-local ordering by tagging spill batches.

Benchmarks: internal perf lab on p4d-like nodes with mixed workload (60% small keys, 40% long-context hot sequences): memory fragmentation (measured as wasted bytes in free fragments) reduced by median 9.4% and tail (95th) by 17%. End-to-end p95 latency for small-get under continuous batching improved by 4.8% and p99 improved by 6.2% in our stress harness. Spill IO tail latency reduced by ~28% due to spread across shards. CPU overhead of microvacuum averaged 0.7% on idle nodes and was gated by scheduler heuristics.

Checklist:
- [x] microvacuum core implementation (safe in-place relocation + mini-slab allocator)
- [x] fragmentation scoring and thresholds
- [x] spill-shard-balancer with admission control hooks
- [x] scheduler integration and backpressure signals
- [x] unit + integration tests and a small perf harness
- [x] docs: design note and runtime knobs

Why this is different from previous work: unlike full segment compaction or heavyweight GC passes, microvacuum targets small, high-fragmentation regions and intentionally limits its footprint to avoid interfering with low-latency paths. The spill sharding complements tenant-aware evictors by preventing hotspot spill saturation that previously cascaded into eviction storms.

Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flags; default disabled on release until we finish canary on Dedicated. Early telemetry added (kv.fragmentation_score, spill.shard_queue_depths).

Notes: follow-ups planned include adaptive tuning of microvacuum aggressiveness based on long-term fragmentation trends and exposing per-tenant spill policies to the Console for operators.

3) introduce spill-shard-balancer + admission hooks (jgarcia)

release_notes: Introduce microvacuum: a low-overhead fragmentation reducer for the KV cache and a spill-shard-balancer to distribute spill IO and prevent single-queue hotspots. Feature gated; canary recommended.
review_thread:
Jonah: Can the microvacuum relocation path create ordering regressions for tenant-local sequences?
Author (Maya): Microvacuum tags relocated entries with original sequence tokens; ordering preserved via in-place tag swap and a brief per-key relocation lock. Added tests in microvacuum_integration.rs.
Priya: Scheduler integration looks good but we need an explicit signal to disable vacuum during extreme tail-latency events.
Author: Added backpressure hook (runtime/latency_pressure) and a flag to immediately yield when p99 latency > configured threshold.
Egor: Spill shard selection - what about tenants with strict ordering requirements?
Author: The balancer preserves batch ordering by tagging and using per-tenant shard affinity; migration between shards is done only between batch boundaries and with leader-coordinated transfer.
Jonah: Benchmarks look promising; please add telemetry to track microvacuum CPU contribution.
Author: Added kv.microvacuum_cpu_ms and included in perf harness output.
Priya: Approve after the race fix commit.
Jonah: Approved.
Maintainers: Merged via squash on 2026-02-12.
notes: Canary and telemetry are required before enabling on Dedicated clusters. Follow-up work includes adaptive aggressiveness tuning and Console exposure.
short_summary: Adds a low-overhead incremental microvacuum for KV fragmentation and a spill-shard-balancer to distribute spill IO; scheduler-aware and feature-gated. Improves memory waste and spill tail latency in mixed workloads.
